sandhi.rule: yaṇ: i → y before an unlike vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), at the prefix junction of abhi + āsa
savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: अभ्यासस्य अतिशयः अभ्यासातिशयः; अभ्यासातिशयेन ज्ञाता अभ्यासातिशयज्ञाता
samasa.vigraha_iast: abhyāsasya atiśayaḥ abhyāsātiśayaḥ; abhyāsātiśayena jñātā abhyāsātiśayajñātā
samasa.explanation: (1) abhyāsa-atiśaya 'the intensity (excess) of practice' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; atiśaya is the head). (2) The participle jñātā 'known' is the head of the whole and takes (1) in the instrumental of means: 'known through intense practice'.

names.meaning: She who is known through intense and sustained spiritual practice
names.significance: The Bhagavad Gītā (6.35) teaches that the restless mind is held by practice (abhyāsa) and dispassion; She is realized when that practice becomes wholehearted and continuous.

meaning_check.note: Typo 'streneous' corrected; 'only' is not in the name.

names.previous_split_issues: jñātā was glossed 'knower/known'; here it is the past participle jñāta 'known' with the feminine -ā, not the agent noun jñātṛ 'knower'.

sandhi.rule: jaśtva: the final ṣ of ṣaṣ 'six' becomes the voiced stop ḍ at the word boundary before a vowel (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte)
savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: possessive in -in over a karmadhāraya, with an inner dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa and dvigu
samasa.vigraha: षट् अध्वानः षडध्वानः; षडध्वनः अतीतम् षडध्वातीतम्; षडध्वातीतम् रूपम् षडध्वातीतरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति षडध्वातीतरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: ṣaṭ adhvānaḥ ṣaḍadhvānaḥ; ṣaḍadhvanaḥ atītam ṣaḍadhvātītam; ṣaḍadhvātītam rūpam ṣaḍadhvātītarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti ṣaḍadhvātītarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) ṣaḍ-adhvan 'the six paths' (dvigu; adhvan drops its n). (2) ṣaḍadhva-atīta 'gone beyond the six paths' (dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa with atīta, Pāṇini 2.1.24). (3) This qualifies rūpa 'form' (karmadhāraya), and the possessive -in (feminine -iṇī) makes the whole describe Her: 'She whose form transcends the six paths'.

components.note: ṣaṭ as a word; ḍ before the vowel by jaśtva

components.meaning: path, way; in Tantra one of the six adhvans

names.meaning: She whose form transcends the six paths
names.significance: In the Āgamas the six adhvans are the six 'paths' by which the cosmos unfolds: varṇa, pada and mantra on the side of sound, and kalā, tattva and bhuvana on the side of objects. Her true form lies beyond all six.
names.previous_split_issues: ṣaḍadhvātīta was left as one row ('beyond the six paths'); it is ṣaṣ 'six' + adhvan 'path' + atīta 'gone beyond'.

sandhi.rule: yaṇ: i → y before an unlike vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), at the prefix junction of vi + āja

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and a nañ-bahuvrīhi)
samasa.vigraha: न विद्यते व्याजः यस्याः सा अव्याजा; अव्याजा करुणा अव्याजकरुणा; अव्याजकरुणायाः मूर्तिः अव्याजकरुणामूर्तिः
samasa.vigraha_iast: na vidyate vyājaḥ yasyāḥ sā avyājā; avyājā karuṇā avyājakaruṇā; avyājakaruṇāyāḥ mūrtiḥ avyājakaruṇāmūrtiḥ
samasa.explanation: (1) a-vyāja 'without pretext or motive' (nañ-bahuvrīhi). (2) It qualifies karuṇā 'compassion' (karmadhāraya; puṃvadbhāva gives avyāja-): 'compassion that needs no reason'. (3) mūrti 'embodiment' is the head and the compassion stands to it in the genitive: 'the embodiment of unconditional compassion'. A karmadhāraya reading ('the form that is itself such compassion') gives the same sense.

names.meaning: She who is the embodiment of compassion that asks for no reason
names.significance: Her compassion does not wait for merit or devotion; it is Her nature, as a mother's love precedes the child's deserving.

meaning_check.note: 'pure compassion' did not render avyāja 'without pretext, unconditional' or mūrti 'embodiment'.

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner rūpaka-karmadhāraya and a nañ-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: न ज्ञानम् अज्ञानम्; अज्ञानम् एव ध्वान्तम् अज्ञानध्वान्तम्; अज्ञानध्वान्तस्य दीपिका अज्ञानध्वान्तदीपिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: na jñānam ajñānam; ajñānam eva dhvāntam ajñānadhvāntam; ajñānadhvāntasya dīpikā ajñānadhvāntadīpikā
samasa.explanation: (1) a-jñāna 'ignorance' (nañ-tatpuruṣa). (2) ajñāna-dhvānta 'the darkness that is ignorance' (karmadhāraya of identification, rūpaka). (3) dīpikā 'lamp' is the head and the darkness stands to it in the genitive: 'the lamp for the darkness of ignorance', i.e. the lamp that dispels it.

components.note: √dhvan, past participle used as a noun

names.meaning: She who is the bright lamp that dispels the darkness of ignorance
names.significance: As one lamp ends the darkness of a room at once, knowledge of Her ends ignorance, however long it has lasted.

samasa.type: avyayībhāva over an itaretara-dvandva, joined to the participle
samasa.vigraha: बालाः च गोपाः च बालगोपाः; आ बालगोपेभ्यः आबालगोपम्; आबालगोपम् विदिता आबालगोपविदिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: bālāḥ ca gopāḥ ca bālagopāḥ; ā bālagopebhyaḥ ābālagopam; ābālagopam viditā ābālagopaviditā
samasa.explanation: (1) bāla-gopa 'children and cowherds' (dvandva). (2) ā 'up to, including' with it forms an avyayībhāva, ābālagopam 'down to children and cowherds' (Pāṇini 2.1.13 āṅ maryādābhividhyoḥ; here inclusive). (3) This qualifies the participle viditā 'known': 'known to all, down to children and cowherds'.

names.meaning: She who is known by all, even by children and cowherds
names.significance: No learning is needed to know Her: even children and cowherds know Her as the Mother, present in every heart.

meaning_check.note: 'well' dropped; 'all' follows from the inclusive ā.

names.previous_split_issues: gopa was glossed 'beetle'; here it is 'cowherd'. ābāla was glossed 'from children'; ā here is inclusive ('down to and including').
names.uncertain: The outer link of the avyayībhāva to the participle viditā is loose; it may also be read as an instrumental, 'known by (all) down to children and cowherds'.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
the prefix ud assimilates to the following l: d becomes l (Pāṇini 8.4.60 tor li)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a nañ-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: न उल्लङ्घ्यम् अनुल्लङ्घ्यम्; सर्वैः अनुल्लङ्घ्यम् सर्वानुल्लङ्घ्यम्; सर्वानुल्लङ्घ्यम् शासनम् यस्याः सा सर्वानुल्लङ्घ्यशासना
samasa.vigraha_iast: na ullaṅghyam anullaṅghyam; sarvaiḥ anullaṅghyam sarvānullaṅghyam; sarvānullaṅghyam śāsanam yasyāḥ sā sarvānullaṅghyaśāsanā
samasa.explanation: (1) an-ullaṅghya 'not to be transgressed' (nañ-tatpuruṣa; na becomes an- before a vowel). (2) sarva-anullaṅghya 'not to be transgressed by anyone' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, the instrumental of the agent with the gerundive). (3) This qualifies śāsana 'command', and the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose command no one can transgress'.

components.note: śāsana (from √śās 'to command'), with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose command no one can transgress
names.significance: Even the gods, the sun, fire and wind act under Her command; the order of the cosmos is Her unbroken law.

meaning_check.note: anullaṅghya is a gerundive, 'not to be transgressed', so the sense is 'cannot be disobeyed', not merely 'is not disobeyed'.

names.previous_split_issues: sarvānullaṅghya was left as one row; it is sarva + an-ud-laṅghya, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: चक्राणाम् राजा चक्रराजः; श्रीयुक्तः चक्रराजः श्रीचक्रराजः; श्रीचक्रराजः निलयः यस्याः सा श्रीचक्रराजनिलया
samasa.vigraha_iast: cakrāṇām rājā cakrarājaḥ; śrīyuktaḥ cakrarājaḥ śrīcakrarājaḥ; śrīcakrarājaḥ nilayaḥ yasyāḥ sā śrīcakrarājanilayā
samasa.explanation: (1) cakra-rāja 'the king of cakras' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; rājan becomes rāja at the end of a tatpuruṣa, Pāṇini 5.4.91 rājāhaḥsakhibhyaṣ ṭac). (2) śrī qualifies it: 'the glorious king of cakras', the Śrīcakra. (3) nilaya 'abode' is identified with it, and the whole describes Her: 'She whose abode is the Śrīcakra, king of cakras'; nilaya takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: appears as rāja at the end of a tatpuruṣa
ni + √lī 'to rest', with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who abides in the Śrīcakra, the king of cakras
names.significance: The Śrīcakra is Her own form as yantra and the supreme diagram of Śrīvidyā worship; the hymn now names it as Her dwelling as it draws to a close.
names.uncertain: The compound can also be read śrī + cakrarāja, 'the glorious king of cakras'; both name the Śrīcakra.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (over an inner saptamī- or ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and a dvigu)
samasa.vigraha: त्रयाणाम् पुराणाम् समाहारः त्रिपुरम्; त्रिपुरे सुन्दरी त्रिपुरसुन्दरी; श्रीमती त्रिपुरसुन्दरी श्रीमत्त्रिपुरसुन्दरी
samasa.vigraha_iast: trayāṇām purāṇām samāhāraḥ tripuram; tripure sundarī tripurasundarī; śrīmatī tripurasundarī śrīmattripurasundarī
samasa.explanation: (1) tri-pura 'the three cities, the three worlds' (dvigu). (2) tripura-sundarī 'the beauty of the three worlds', i.e. the most beautiful in them (saptamī-tatpuruṣa; a genitive reading gives the same sense). (3) śrīmatī 'glorious' qualifies her, reduced to śrīmat by puṃvadbhāva in the karmadhāraya: 'the glorious Tripurasundarī'.

names.meaning: She who is the glorious Tripurasundarī
names.significance: Tripurasundarī is the presiding name of the Goddess in Śrīvidyā, the most beautiful in the three worlds and beyond the three states of waking, dream and sleep.

meaning_check.note: 'divine tripurasundarI devI' put into IAST and tightened; 'devī' is not in the name.

samasa.explanation: śrī 'auspicious, glorious' stands in apposition to śivā 'the auspicious one, Śiva's consort': 'the auspicious Śivā'. The members meet without sound change.

components.meaning: Śivā: the auspicious one, the consort of Śiva

names.meaning: She who is the auspicious and divine Śivā
names.significance: She is Śivā, the power of Śiva and auspiciousness itself; the next name declares Śiva and Śakti to be one.
names.previous_split_issues: śivā was glossed 'Shiva'; it is the feminine Śivā, the auspicious Goddess.

sandhi.rule: yaṇ: i → y before an unlike vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

samasa.type: possessive in -in over a karmadhāraya, a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and an itaretara-dvandva
samasa.vigraha: शिवः च शक्तिः च शिवशक्ती; शिवशक्त्योः ऐक्यम् शिवशक्त्यैक्यम्; शिवशक्त्यैक्यम् एव रूपम् शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: śivaḥ ca śaktiḥ ca śivaśaktī; śivaśaktyoḥ aikyam śivaśaktyaikyam; śivaśaktyaikyam eva rūpam śivaśaktyaikyarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti śivaśaktyaikyarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) śiva-śakti 'Śiva and Śakti' (itaretara-dvandva). (2) śivaśakti-aikya 'the oneness of Śiva and Śakti' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) That oneness is identified with rūpa 'form', and the possessive -in (feminine -iṇī) makes the whole describe Her: 'She whose form is the union of Śiva and Śakti'.

names.meaning: She who is the union of Śiva and Śakti in one form
names.significance: The whole of Śrīvidyā rests on this non-duality: Śiva without Śakti cannot act, Śakti without Śiva has no ground; Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī are one.
names.previous_split_issues: The old split read śaktaikya (the text then lacked the y); the members are śakti + aikya, joined by yaṇ (the text was corrected to शक्त्यैक्य).

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: ललिता च असौ अम्बिका च ललिताम्बिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: lalitā ca asau ambikā ca lalitāmbikā
samasa.explanation: Lalitā and ambikā 'Mother' are co-referential: 'Lalitā, the Mother'. ambikā is the head; the two simply meet in savarṇa-dīrgha.

components.meaning: Lalitā: 'She who plays', the lovely one

names.meaning: She who is the divine Mother Lalitā
names.significance: The thousand names end with Her own name: Lalitā, whose play is the universe, and Ambikā, the Mother to whom every name has been addressed.

external_sandhi.rule: visarga after a vowel other than a/ā becomes r before a voiced sound (here the vowel a)

verse_notes.note: The r before ajñāna belongs to name 992 (mūrtiḥ); name 993 begins ajñāna. Name 991's 'six paths' are the six adhvans of the Āgamas.

Name 994: gopa is 'cowherd' (not 'beetle'), and ā- is inclusive, 'down to'. Names 996–997 name the Śrīcakra and Tripurasundarī, the yantra and the presiding deity of Śrīvidyā, as the hymn closes; 997 is spelled with tt (śrīmat + tripura).

The first half holds the last three names, 998–1000, ending on Her own name, Lalitāmbikā. The second half is not a name but the closing line (its words are analysed below). Traditionally the singers are the Vāgdevīs (Vaśinī and the others), who composed the hymn at Her command.

report.summary: Checked the last 11 names (990–1000, ślokas 181–183) against text.json, with sandhi at every member and prefix junction, layered vigraha-vākyas in pausa form, and every meaning against the analysis; the closing half-line of śloka 183 is explained in its verse note. Two members were misidentified in the old tables (994 gopa 'beetle' for 'cowherd'; 990 jñātā as 'knower' rather than 'known'), and 992's meaning was sharpened to render avyāja 'without any pretext' and mūrti 'embodiment'. No problem was found in the Sanskrit of the names; the only observation is spacing in the closing line (श्रीललिता देव्या reads as one compound), noted in the verse note.
